endorsements.quote: Regardless of development approach, clinicians must independently evaluate whether recommendations and their underlying source material are appropriate for the patient at hand.
Apply makes explicit that responsibility for clinical decisions cannot be delegated to AI systems, even when their recommendations are followed.

After considering AI-enabled input, clinicians integrate the information and recommendations with the patient\u2019s values, competing risks, local context, and clinical judgment, then commit to a final plan and document their reasoning in their own words.

unlisted_practices: Clinicians should formulate queries to AI-enabled CDS tools by clearly specifying the clinical question, relevant patient context, and purpose of the interaction.
Clinicians should evaluate the evidentiary basis, recommendation strength, and transparency of AI-generated recommendations when available.
Clinicians should rely more heavily on independent verification and external sources when AI does not provide information on evidentiary basis or recommendation strength.
Clinicians should check whether an AI tool's methods statement indicates retrieval from evidence-based curated content or from non-curated content.
Clinicians should recognize when AI output extends beyond validated indications or relevant patient populations.
Trainees should maintain a low threshold for tracing AI citations and consulting additional sources while developing experience to calibrate trust.

screen.reason: This is an editorial proposing the 'Ask-Audit-Apply' framework as a conceptual, clinician-facing framework for clinical reasoning and governance when using AI CDS tools.
